topic: AI use vs. revenue per employee
angle: Usage without redesigning work doesn’t move the P&L; value shows up when processes, KPIs, and incentives change.
sourceTitle: Buried in OpenAI’s latest research: No correlation between AI use and revenue per employee—yet
linkedinPost:
Tough but necessary data point: more AI use isn’t showing up as more revenue per employee—yet.

Fortune highlighted research suggesting no clear link between corporate AI usage and revenue per headcount right now. That’s a wake-up call for anyone equating “seat licenses” with outcomes.

My take from the front lines: AI only moves the P&L when you redesign the work around it. If you add an assistant but keep the same processes, SLAs, and incentives, you’ve just created a shinier status quo.

Where value starts to appear:
- Process surgery: remove steps, not just accelerate them.
- KPI rewiring: measure cycle time, first-contact resolution, and deflection you trust—then tie bonuses to them.
- Decision rights: let frontline teams use AI outputs to close loops without escalation.
- Decommissioning: turn off legacy reports and queues AI replaces.

If you’re not willing to change how work is measured and governed, more usage data won’t rescue ROI. AI is a tool; operating model change is the lever.

How have you changed incentives or processes to make AI show up in financials? #AIAdoption #EnterpriseAI #AIStrategy #AITransformation
xPost: AI “usage” ≠ ROI. Value shows up when you redesign work: cut steps, rewire KPIs, push decision rights down, and decommission what AI replaces. No ops change, no P&L change. #EnterpriseAI #AIAdoption
